body:
Two more observations:
- I wonder if we could also flatten that `InvocationTargetException` a bit (by catching it in `QuarkusTestExtension` and only using its `cause`)?
- `TestResourceManager` is not closed in this case.

> * `TestResourceManager` is not closed in this case.

This not true, see: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/728e5859671d512d4afc73a9f3aacd06fe4d365f/test-framework/junit5/src/main/java/io/quarkus/test/junit/QuarkusTestExtension.java#L245

> > * `TestResourceManager` is not closed in this case.
> 
> This not true

Ah, sorry - missed that block somehow.

https://github.com/maschoene/quarkus-quickstarts/commit/c35a18c90a7736484289e3dc951dab2607d15d3f

```
    @Override
    public Map<String, String> start() {
        LoggerFactory.getLogger(CustomQuarkusTestResourceLifecycleManager.class).error("Recvd error, throwing RTE");
        throw new RuntimeException("RTE");
    }
```

I'd expect `Recvd error, throwing RTE` as well, but only got:
```
[INFO] Running org.acme.getting.started.GreetingResourceTest
[ERROR] Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 1, Skipped: 1, Time elapsed: 9.875 s <<< FAILURE! - in org.acme.getting.started.GreetingResourceTest
[ERROR] testHelloEndpoint  Time elapsed: 0.032 s  <<< ERROR!
java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException
Caused by: java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException
Caused by: java.lang.RuntimeException: Unable to start Quarkus test resource org.acme.getting.started.CustomQuarkusTestResourceLifecycleManager@700b9e6b
Caused by: java.lang.RuntimeException: RTE

[INFO]
[INFO] Results:
[INFO]
[ERROR] Errors:
[ERROR]   GreetingResourceTest.testHelloEndpoint � Runtime java.lang.reflect.InvocationT...
[INFO]
[ERROR] Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 1, Skipped: 1
```

Logging doesn't work properly in this context. 

So if you need more information, you need to add it to the exception you throw.

I'll close this, as it does work as expected. If you feel otherwise, feel free to comment and/or reopen.

If you take a look at the code of the Quarkus JUnit extension, you'll see no place where we log information and for good reason 😉.

As for the javadoc, I agree, it would be nice to have, so if you want to do it, it will be a nice addition
I hope if you don't mind when I reopen this and assign it to me for the JavaDoc adjustment.

issue.title: Clarify in JavaDoc that logging does not work in test LifecycleManager
